subject: Science
title: Class 8 Science Olympiad — Paper 5
instructions: The time allowed for this paper is 60 minutes.
This paper contains 50 objective-type (multiple-choice) questions carrying a total of 60 marks.
There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
Each question has four options; choose the one correct answer.
Section 1 and other regular sections carry 1 mark per question; the Achievers Section carries 3 marks per question.
Use of calculators is not permitted unless specified.

questions.question: If 5 pumps can empty a tank in 8 hours, how many hours will 10 pumps take?
Five children are ranked by age. Mira is older than Tara but younger than Neha. Sara is the youngest. Who could be the oldest?
options: Neha (or someone older, but Neha is oldest among named)

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 8, 16, 32, __
If in a code, LAMP is written as MBNQ, how is DESK written?

Arrange in order of increasing hardness: Wax, Wood, Iron, Diamond

What is the SI unit of pressure?
Which type of energy conversion takes place in a bulb (electric to light)?
options: Electrical to light and heat energy

questions.question: What is the term for the period of rapid physical and emotional change in humans, usually starting around age 11-19?
options: Puberty (a part of adolescence, but adolescence is the broader term)

options: A physical change with no energy release

options: Accumulation and discharge of electric charges in clouds

Which type of lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
options: Bifocal lens with only convex power

questions.question: What is the process of internal fertilisation followed by development inside the mother's body called, as seen in humans?
What is the process of separating grain from chaff called?
What is 'ozone layer depletion' primarily caused by?
Which method of conservation involves protecting a specific area for wildlife?
What is the term for a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern?
Which method is used to remove husk from grains?
What is the main cause of water pollution from industries?
options: Discharge of untreated chemical waste into water bodies

questions.question: Which celestial body is closest to Earth?
Which part of the cell controls all its activities?

What is the zone of a flame that is the hottest?
Which microorganism is used to make curd from milk?
Which of these is a natural fibre?
A biogas plant is set up in a village to convert cattle dung into fuel. Which type of microorganism plays the key role in this process, and what is the primary product?
options: Anaerobic bacteria that decompose organic waste to produce methane-rich biogas
Fungi that produce only carbon dioxide

questions.question: A farmer rotates different crops each season instead of growing the same crop repeatedly. Analyze the scientific reasoning behind this practice.
options: Crop rotation replenishes soil nutrients and reduces the build-up of pests/diseases specific to one crop
It is done purely for tradition with no scientific basis
It only saves the farmer time
It has no effect on soil quality

questions.question: A student wants to test if a liquid conducts electricity using a simple circuit with an LED. If the LED lights up, what can be concluded, and what real-world application does this principle have?
options: No conclusion can be drawn from this test
The liquid is pure water with no dissolved substances
The liquid contains ions/is an electrolyte; this principle is used in electroplating and testing water purity

questions.question: During a lunar eclipse, the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon. Using your understanding of light and shadows, explain why the Moon appears reddish during a total lunar eclipse.
options: The Moon changes its own color
The Sun turns red during eclipses
The Moon absorbs all light except red
Sunlight bends through Earth's atmosphere and scatters, allowing only red wavelengths to reach the Moon

questions.question: A student notices that a wooden block held underwater rises to the surface when released, while a stone sinks. Explain this difference using the concept of buoyancy and density.
options: Both should sink since gravity acts on both
Stone floats due to its shape only
Wood is less dense than water so buoyant force exceeds its weight, while stone is denser so its weight exceeds buoyant force
Wood floats because it has no weight
